summary: Coventry lookout, a 65-ft steel tower first operated in 1926 (a 1923 report already lists the station). Decommissioned 1973; moved to the Cranston Adult Correction Institution as a guard tower.

facts.status_note: Decommissioned in 1973 and moved to the Adult Correction Institution in Cranston, where the register says it is used as a guard tower. The Coventry site is listed as gone; no source describes what remains there.
facts.agency: Rhode Island Commissioner of Forestry, later the Department of Agriculture and Conservation

access.note: Register places the tower at the Adult Correction Institution in Cranston, where it is used as a guard tower; no source describes public access there. No source describes access at the Coventry site.

corrections.why: The register says the tower was moved in 1973 to the Adult Correction Institution in Cranston, where it is used as a guard tower. The Coventry site itself is gone.

corrections.proposed: Rhode Island Commissioner of Forestry, later the Department of Agriculture and Conservation
corrections.why: District 2 is a district label printed on the source page, not an agency. The annual reports quoted there are from the Commissioner of Forestry (1923) and the Department of Agriculture and Conservation (1950, 1951).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1923 Commissioner of Forestry report lists Bowen Hill among five stations set up by then, while the register gives 1926 as the first year of operation. No source we read explains the three-year gap, so the record keeps both dates.
The FFLA list places Bowen Hill at 41.71576, -71.70918, about 0.2 km from the register's point at 41.71667, -71.70717. The record keeps the register's coordinates.

notes_for_editor: The move to the Cranston Adult Correction Institution rests on the register alone; a single search found no second source. The 1923 and 1926 dates conflict and are both kept. The 'District 2' label may denote a forest district rather than an agency; the agency correction is a judgment. Nothing describes the Coventry site today. Brief's 'access unknown' could be filled from the Cranston guard-tower note, but no public access is documented.
